139.76389,35.67686.name: Intuitive Surgical Japan
139.76389,35.67686.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-0.55761,51.31451.name: Care Fertility Woking
-0.55761,51.31451.state: 5 Hillview Road, Woking, Surrey, GU22 7HW, United Kingdom
-0.55761,51.31451.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-73.94529,45.43184.name: McGill University
-73.94529,45.43184.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, September 2023
-73.94529,45.43184.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, September 2023. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

7.88100,46.29400.name: Lonza
7.88100,46.29400.desc: The largest contract manufacturer of biologics in the world, making other companies’ medicines including at pandemic scale. Which products get made, and when, is decided in commercial negotiations between a contractor and its clients. During a shortage that is a rationing decision, taken privately, by a company no health authority appoints or oversees.

0.18400,52.08050.name: European Bioinformatics Institute — model organism databases
0.18400,52.08050.desc: The public databases holding genome and model-organism data for the whole field, run as European infrastructure and free to use. Every argument about sequence ownership and benefit-sharing runs through the fact that this data is already open: material collected in one country is deposited here and readable by anyone, which is the practical reason the Nagoya negotiations on digital sequence information have gone on so long.

-89.40600,43.07500.name: Open Source Seed Initiative
-89.40600,43.07500.desc: Releases varieties under a pledge that they and anything bred from them stay free to use, save and breed with — the seed equivalent of an open source licence, and the direct counter to the technology agreement a patented seed comes with. Several hundred varieties are released this way. It is small against the commercial seed market and it is the only mechanism that puts a variety permanently beyond enclosure rather than merely outside it for now.

1.44420,43.60470.name: Ceva Santé Animale
1.44420,43.60470.desc: A vectored vaccine is an engineered organism by construction: a gene from one organism is inserted into the genome of a virus, which is then given to the animal alive. This company runs a line of thirteen such vaccines built on fowlpox virus and on herpesvirus of turkeys, carrying antigens for Newcastle disease, infectious bursal disease, infectious laryngotracheitis, avian influenza and Mycoplasma gallisepticum. Its Newcastle product inserts the virus's fusion gene into the turkey herpesvirus genome, with the insertion site and promoter patented. These go into commercial poultry at a scale nothing else on this map approaches, and frequently in ovo — injected into the egg before the bird has hatched. The industry treats them as vaccines and the biosafety literature treats them as recombinant organisms, and both descriptions are accurate at once.
